must_find.description: The search term is interpolated into the SQL string, so the caller can run arbitrary statements.
The new search route carries no guard, while the route beside it in the same controller does.

acceptable.description: Every column of the customer table is selected and returned, so personal data leaves the service and a future column joins the response on its own.
The query has no limit, so a common term returns the whole table.

must_not_flag.description: Objecting to raw SQL inside a repository in the infrastructure layer. That is where raw SQL belongs; the problem here is the interpolation, not the SQL.
Demanding an index for the pattern match. Nothing in the diff shows the table's indexes, so this is a guess about code that was not provided.

notes: The first sample whose diff modifies files rather than adding them, which matters because the authorization finding is only visible in a context line: the guard on the route above is unchanged, so a reviewer that reads added lines alone cannot see the asymmetry. Also the set's only injection case, and its strictest band - critical only, because rating this anything less is a calibration failure rather than a judgement call.
